# 2 Baruch Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**10:1** "Blessed is-the-one-who-was-not-born, or-he-who-having-been-born has-died.

**10:2** But-as-for-us-the-living, woe-to-us, because-we-see-the-afflictions-of-Zion and-what-has-befallen-Jerusalem.

**10:3** I-will-call-up the-sirens from-the-sea, and-you-night-spectres come-from-the-desert, and-you-demons and-jackals from-the-forests: wake-ye-and-gird-your-loins-for-mourning and-take-up-with-me-a-lamentation.

**10:4** And-do-not-mourn-for-me, O-Zion; [rather] mourn-for-thyself, O-Zion; for the-desolation-of-the-Comforter-[who-was] near-you.

**10:5** For-the-righteous-have-been-taken-away and-the-prophets-have-gone-to-sleep, and-we-have-gone-forth from-our-land and-Zion-has-been-taken-away from-us, and-we-have-nothing-now save-only-the-Mighty-One and-his-law.

**10:6** If-therefore-we-have-put-away-from-our-heart-all-our-vanity and-have-directed-our-heart-to-the-Mighty-One, he-will-restore-to-us again-all-that-we-have-lost, and-multiply it-for-us-many-times.

**10:7** But-the-righteous-of-these-days, for-righteousness-is-their-portion, they-shall-rejoice and-not-be-ashamed.

**10:8** And-they-whose-fathers-have-been-taught-wisdom [shall]-receive their-wages; and-they-who-have-been-ruled [by]-men of-understanding shall-not-be-removed.

**10:9** But-now we-are-called-by-this-name, which-we-had-inherited-from-our-fathers, and-yet-we-have-become-estranged-from-our-inheritance.

**10:10** What-therefore shall-we-say-to-those-who-are-at-rest in-Babylon, or-to-those-who-have-been-scattered-there?

**10:11** For-Zion-has-been-taken-away-from-us, and-we-have-no-[other]-place-of-refuge.

**10:12** And-we-have-left-our-land, and-we-have-no-inheritance-now in-other-lands.

**10:13** Now, O-ye-brides, do-not-enter the-bridal-chambers; and-ye-virgins, weave-not-your-garlands; and-ye-wives, pray-not-for-children;

**10:14** And-ye-who-are-with-child, pray-not-that-ye-may-be-delivered; for-the-barren-shall-rather-rejoice, and-those-who-have-no-sons shall-exult, and-those-who-have-sons shall-be-grieved.

**10:15** For-why-should-men-beget-children, if-they-are-to-be-given-over-to-Sheol?

**10:16** Or-why-should-the-human-race-continue, if-it-is-to-come-to-destruction?

**10:17** Or-why-should-man-rule over-his-household, if-he-is-to-be-bereaved?

**10:18** Or-why-should-there-be-travail [in]-giving-birth, if-the-fruits-of-the-womb-are-to-be-cut-off before-they-are-ripe?

**10:19** Or-why-should-one-put-on-the-splendor-of-virginity, or-adorn-himself-with-beauty, when-it-is-destined-to-be-brought-to-naught in-Sheol?"

---

*EMET notes: Baruch's great lament. V.1 echoes Job 3 ("blessed is he who was not born"). The summons to mythological mourners (v.3) is a unique apocalyptic image. The "what profit is begetting?" series (vv.15-19) parallels Eccl and Job.*
